title: Learning to read and bass lessons
summary: He faked at first, got some reading from Dave Jackson, and got ideas and fingerboard instruction from older bassists.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. I wonder if you could tell us a little bit about the bass, what you, when did you learn to read? You say you started out without learning to read.
Yeah, I started out with faking, yeah. A little reading I'd done, a little learning I got. I started at Dave, at Old Man Jackson. Yeah.
Had anybody, uh, 34 years in there. Had anybody given you any lessons at all, even about playing the bass in New Orleans?
Oh yeah, sure, oh, I got a lot of, a lot of lessons, um, I got a lot of ideas from real good bass players. Like I told you, this Henry Kimmel. Yeah. He actually showed you the thing rings.
He actually showed you the thing rings to read him.
He said, Dave, listen. Yeah, he's a thing ring. He showed me how to use this. E string, which I know he'd use before. I take it off, but it was in my way. Too many strings.
But he didn't teach you to read them?

No, he just teached me the fingerboard, you know, and I went on. And, uh, lots of different bass players, older bass players than I was, more experienced than I was, give me a lot of ideas, showed me, you know.
